headline: A Goldman Sachs index that leaves out AI-related companies has gained far less than the S&P 500 over the past six months, showing how much the record rests on AI.
score_reason: Read in full via a copy site; data are specific and dated 6 Oct 2026. No reduction.
importance_line: Anyone holding US index funds is more tied to AI shares than it may seem, since the index's records now rest on AI-linked stocks.
summary: BeInCrypto reports, in a version on Yahoo Finance and citing Axios and CNBC, that the S&P 500 has gained 18.3% in six months, while Goldman Sachs' index excluding AI enablers, built in February to let clients hedge AI exposure, gained 6.7% and sits 6.4% below its high. Goldman counts about 45% of the S&P 500 as AI enablers, and one fund manager cited says the next phase of the trade could be power producers.
notes: Original is BeInCrypto (link not in chunk); text read on Yahoo Finance. Chain: BeInCrypto citing Axios (index) and CNBC (chip gains).
